one_sentence_story: When Edward Deci paid students for one session to assemble 3D Soma puzzle cubes they already enjoyed, they dropped the puzzles like a chore the moment pay stopped — because dangling 'if-then' rewards shifts your brain's story from 'I love this' to 'I only do this when paid.'
so_what_for_you: Protect activities people naturally love from tiny piece-rate bribes: pay people generously at baseline, then fuel curiosity with autonomy and specific mastery feedback rather than per-task carrots.

jargon_map.plain: losing natural enjoyment for an activity after an expected external reward takes over as your reason for doing it
jargon_map.analogy: like forgetting you loved gardening once someone pays you by the weed pulled

jargon_map.plain: doing an activity purely because the challenge itself feels satisfying
jargon_map.analogy: like solving a Sunday crossword on a train with nobody watching

jargon_map.plain: whether your brain perceives an action as freely chosen inside you or pulled by strings outside you
jargon_map.analogy: like steering your own sailboat vs being towed by a rope

jargon_map.plain: specific praise showing growing skill versus 'do this to earn a prize' pressure
jargon_map.analogy: like a coach timing your personal best vs dangling a voucher
